operations.text: Click a visible pixel in the input preview or enter HEX. Protection keeps the assigned reference from the active library (full master in original mode) in the selected palette; its RGB may differ from your original. Protected colours count towards the limit.
Protect selected source colours

Uses the HEX above. Here, “original” means the frozen, browser-decoded sRGB input, not the channels stored in the image file. Keeps every matching visible pixel in the frozen, browser-decoded input exactly, including alpha. Each original reserves one palette slot separately from protected references. No tolerance, no area mask. Other colours can still become the same output RGB.
Protect colours in a rectangle

All frozen, browser-decoded RGB nuances and alpha inside each rectangle stay exact. Their distinct visible RGB values reserve palette slots. If protection exceeds the limit, the preview stops and asks you to increase it or reduce the protected area. Outside colours can still become the same output RGB.

The loupe shows frozen, browser-decoded sRGB RGB/RGBA8 values. In original mode, original RGB and rectangle protection preserve these values exactly. In library mode, selected colours are converted to library references and then fixed. Browser decoding may change stored file channels, especially with partial transparency; it does not guarantee identical numbers to the PNG file. The outlined centre is selected. Click a magnified pixel or use the arrows to refine your selection.

Compare variants

Drag any comparison panel to move all three views together. These views do not change pixels or export settings.

Hover or tap a comparison image to inspect one source pixel. Arrow keys move the selected pixel.

Markers, magnifiers and overlays are inspection aids only; exported image pixels are unchanged. Saved variants show their own reduction, cleanup and protection settings.

Correct and protect an area

Use after the first reduction. Hover or tap a pixel in the current comparison and set each corner below, or enter source-pixel coordinates. Suggestions always come from the original source, never the distorted output. Save a variant first if you want to compare the previous palette.

Create a reduced preview first.

Both rectangle edges are included. Corrected visible pixels are fixed during cleanup under either scope; alpha stays unchanged. Recalculation can change unlocked colours elsewhere. Corrections must not overlap. Changing the library or mode, or loading another source, clears corrections. Original pixels and full-master assignments stay separate.

Clean up unprotected areas

Palette locks always retain their references during reduction. For cleanup, choose whether their pixels everywhere are protected too, or only pixels explicitly selected through source-colour locks and rectangles. Exact original RGB entries always remain protected.

Simplifies small connected colour islands using existing palette colours. Selected pixel areas stay unchanged. The scope control determines whether protected palette colours are also protected everywhere. Alpha is preserved. Each application starts from the reduced preview, so cleanup does not accumulate.

Selected output palette

Export up to 256 selected output entries. In original mode, exact originals are labelled separately from Atlas reference swatches. Clarus JSON chunks contain references only; use the full ZIP for original RGB evidence.

The ZIP retains the original image file byte-for-byte, separately from frozen, browser-decoded input pixels, Atlas assignments, reduced PNG and palette. In reduction.json, file_sha256 identifies the original file; input_rgba_sha256 identifies the frozen pixels. The manifest checksums cover the exported files. Keep it for handover. It is a reduction evidence package, not an editable Image Projects ZIP.
